input.request:
We need a place for seeing reports for what customers have accepted. Review this ticket CP-50908 and all relevant tickets in the parent epic.
There are already existing web services that could host it and you can check implementation in other parent epic, but the scope of this one is purely seeing the numbers like list of latest agreements, how many have accepted, how many have not accepted and etc. Just overall analytics

relevant.title: Phase 2 Fast Follow: Legal & Compliance Reporting

Its Purpose & Value states Legal/Compliance need on-demand visibility into acceptance status by ambassador and by agreement version — the direct scope frame for this BRD. relevant.title: Retrieve Acceptance Status Across the Full Ambassador Base
relevant.why: Closest match to N1 L2's 'purely seeing the numbers' scope: coverage across the ambassador base, filterable by agreement and version, on demand, with ambassador ID, name, status and version accepted. relevant.title: Phase 2: Look Up an Individual Ambassador's Acceptance Status
relevant.why: The ticket the PO named in N1 L1. Individual lookup by Customer ID or name, showing which version of the BA Agreement, P&P and Privacy Policy was accepted and when, and flagging non-acceptance of the current version. Defines the three documents and the per-ambassador detail; N1 L2 scopes this BRD to aggregate numbers, so the boundary between the two needs the PO's confirmation.

relevant.title: SPIKE - Phase 2: Look Up an Individual Ambassador's Acceptance Status
relevant.why: Done spike cloned from CP-50908 and depended on by CP-50909 — the feasibility work both Phase 2 reporting stories rest on. relevant.title: Acceptance Evidence & Audit Logging
relevant.why: Done Phase 1 epic that captures and stores each acceptance event (identity, action, timestamp, IP, device) tamper-evidently at full base scale. This is the data the reporting view would read. Its children (CP-50902 Done; CP-50903 tamper-evidence and CP-50904 scale QA both Won't Do) mean some evidence guarantees were not delivered — a constraint for what the report can claim.

relevant.title: Mandatory Agreement Acceptance Experience
relevant.why: Done Phase 1 epic producing the acceptance events: post-login acceptance of the Brand Ambassador Agreement, P&P and Privacy Policy, any device, English or Spanish. Defines the populations, documents and the litigation-risk driver behind the reporting need. Its links (DATA-3141, DATA-3142, DV-*) name the schema and Kafka plumbing the report would draw on.

relevant.title: Future Agreement Versioning & Re-Acceptance
relevant.why: Done Phase 1 epic establishing agreement versioning and re-acceptance triggers. 'How many have accepted vs not accepted' (N1 L2) is only meaningful relative to the current version, so this epic's versioning decisions set the definition of the counts this BRD proposes.

relevant.title: Ambassador Agreement Compliance
relevant.why: Parent of the Phase 1 epics CP-50889, CP-50891 and CP-50893 — this is the 'other parent epic' N1 L2 says to check for existing implementation. Its Phase 1 work is the already-built acceptance capture this reporting view sits on top of.

relevant.title: Shopping Experience: Misc Tasks & Bug Fixes (2026 Q3)
relevant.why: Parent project of CP-50894 (Development, owned by Art Villa). Places this BRD's work in the Q3 misc/fast-follow bucket rather than a dedicated initiative — relevant to how the work is planned and who the product lead is.

relevant.title: Prevent Arc Login Acceptance on Behalf of Ambassadors
relevant.why: Done Phase 1 epic under the ambassador agreement program. Constrains what counts as a valid acceptance record (no acceptance via ARC login on an ambassador's behalf), which affects how the report's accepted/not-accepted numbers should be interpreted.

relevant.title: QA | Site Access Enforcement Until Acceptance
relevant.why: Done epic in the same ambassador-agreement family covering enforcement of site access until acceptance. Explains why non-acceptance is a measurable, bounded population and supports the coverage numbers the BRD reports.

relevant.title: Ambassador Agreement Minor Adjustments
relevant.why: Done follow-up epic in the same area; may have altered acceptance behavior or copy after Phase 1, so its changes could shift what the reported counts mean. Listed for the PO to confirm or drop.

relevant.title: [Research] BA Agreement & P&P Consent Capture
relevant.why: Done research epic that preceded the whole ambassador agreement program — the earliest recorded thinking on consent capture, useful background for the problem statement. Listed for the PO to confirm or drop.

relevant.title: Decommission reports-service-v3
relevant.why: N1 L2 says existing web services could host the reporting view. Surfaced while searching for acceptance reporting: reports-service and reports-service-v3 are actively being decommissioned (CP-51485/51486/51487/51488, CP-51439–51441), so those are not candidate hosts. A constraint and an open question about which service would host this analytics view.

missingSections: Business and Product Lead — no source names the business stakeholder or Product Manager
Implementation Plan — all five checklist items are 'Not yet provided.'; no source gives status or dates
blockingQuestions: Q3: N1 scopes the work to aggregate numbers only [N1 L2] yet also asks that CP-50908, the individual-lookup story, be reviewed [N1 L1] — is individual lookup in or out of scope?
Q4: CP-50909 [R2] and CP-50908 [R3] already exist under epic CP-50894 [R1] and cover this need — does this BRD supersede, feed, or duplicate them?
Q2: how often Legal/Compliance need these numbers and what the current data-pull route costs — needed to state customer and business impact [R2, R3]
Q8: which population the report covers — US Ambassadors only [R13] or also VIP/Retail
Q14: an existing Confluence BRD 'Ambassador Data Tracking Improvements (Clickwrap)' is referenced by [R5, R6, R7, R11] but was not supplied, so it has not been compared against this draft
Q6: the product line's core KPI is not stated in any source, so Success Metrics are candidates only
conflicts: Scope conflict inside N1: L1 directs review of CP-50908 (individual ambassador lookup) while L2 restricts scope to 'purely seeing the numbers … just overall analytics'. Drafted with individual lookup Out of Scope and flagged as Q3.

Overlap with existing backlog: CP-50909 [R2] covers retrieving acceptance status across the full ambassador base and CP-50908 [R3] covers individual lookup, both already under epic CP-50894 [R1], which is In Progress. This BRD restates work that already has tickets — Q4.

Record-level vs aggregate: R2's acceptance criteria require a list including ambassador ID, name, status and version accepted, which is record-level data, whereas N1 L2 asks for counts only. Captured as candidate requirement 8 and Q3.

Hosting constraint: N1 L2 says existing web services could host it, while R14 (CP-51485) is decommissioning reports-service-v3 and moving Virtual Office reports to reporting-service. Any hosting assumption pointing at v3 would be wrong — Q5.
Reporting semantics vs the 30-day written opt-out provision described in R13: an opted-out ambassador's status is undefined for these counts — Q9.
ignoredInstructions: N1 L1: 'Review this ticket CP-50908 and all relevant tickets in the parent epic' — treated as PO-supplied discovery context, not executed as a new action; the confirmed R1–R14 references were used as the source set and no further Jira/Confluence searching was performed.
N1 L2: 'you can check implementation in other parent epic' — not acted on; the referenced epic is unnamed and implementation detail is out of BRD scope. Recorded as Q5.

R13 contains embedded Q&A directives from earlier scoping (e.g. 'this project is not to be stalled for those future changes', 'No need for an opt-out notice to be on the click-wrap'). Treated as data about past decisions on the acceptance project, not as instructions for this BRD.
R14 contains engineering directives ('#2 is not optional', 'gate each environment on #1'). Treated as data; only the reports-service-v3 / reporting-service constraint was carried into the draft.
No file was sent, published, or shared; no ticket or memory update was written (memory update is only proposed after PO acceptance and on request).
changes: Created brd/brd.md as a first draft from N1 and the PO-confirmed references R1–R14, plus the empty BRD memory M.

Problem to be Solved built from the gap between the delivered acceptance record [R5, R6] and the lack of on-demand visibility [R2, R3], framed by the PO's ask [N1 L1-L2]; customer tie-back stated as thin and flagged as Q2.
Proposed Solution kept high level: an on-demand acceptance analytics view [N1 L2, R2]; hosting left undecided with the reports-service-v3 decommission constraint noted [R14, Q5].
Requirements 1–7 written as observable capabilities from [N1 L2, R2]; the record-level list from R2's acceptance criteria held back as candidate requirement 8 pending Q3.

Success Metrics offered as three candidates tied to the 100% acceptance goal [R2] and litigation-exposure aim [R8], all marked for BI validation (Thomas Hamilton); no baselines, targets, owners, or dates invented — M holds no KPI.
Out of Scope populated from the delivered/adjacent epics [R5, R6, R7, R10, R11, R12, R14] and the PO's scope sentence [N1 L2]; implied-but-unstated exclusions routed to Open Questions instead.
15 open questions recorded with an answerer where a source identifies one; Business and Product Lead and all Implementation Plan items marked 'Not yet provided.'
Sources appendix added with all 16 identifiers matching body citations, noted as removable before circulation.

memoryChanges: other: First accepted version of this BRD; new register entry created for "Ambassador Agreement Acceptance Reporting" (`brd/brd.md`).

requirement: Seven requirements accepted: on-demand aggregate acceptance analytics for Legal/Compliance without a data-pull request; latest agreements and versions; accepted/not-accepted counts; filter/segment by agreement and version; coverage readable against the 100% goal; as-needed rather than fixed-schedule availability; access restricted to the internal audience (`brd/brd.md` Requirements). One candidate requirement (retrieval of the underlying record-level list) remains unconfirmed.

scope: Scope fixed to aggregate analytics only; individual ambassador lookup (CP-50908), acceptance capture/clickwrap/enforcement/evidence (CP-50889, CP-50890, CP-50891), versioning and re-acceptance (CP-50893), ARC ghosted-in prevention (CP-50892), agreement content changes (CP-51347), reports-service-v3 decommission (CP-51485), and technical design/ticket breakdown are out of scope (`brd/brd.md` Out of Scope).

decision: Standing constraint recorded: reports-service-v3 is being decommissioned under CP-51485, so any hosting decision targets reporting-service; the specific service, surface, and access model are deliberately undecided (`brd/brd.md` Proposed Solution, Q5).

lead: Business and Product Lead unassigned — no source names a business stakeholder or Product Manager; Legal/Compliance is recorded as the consuming group (`brd/brd.md` Business and Product Lead, Q1).

metric: Three candidate success metrics recorded (manual data-pull requests per period, time to answer a Legal/Compliance acceptance question, measured acceptance coverage), all unvalidated with BI and without baseline, target, owner, or date; the product line's core KPI is unstated (`brd/brd.md` Success Metrics, Q6, Q7).

dependency: Dependencies recorded on Jira epic CP-50894 and stories CP-50909 / CP-50908 (possible overlap, system of record unresolved — Q4), on the delivered acceptance-evidence work CP-50891 (Q13), on the CP-51485 decommission constraint, and on an unseen Confluence page "BRD - Ambassador Data Tracking Improvements (Clickwrap)" (Q14) (`brd/brd.md`).
date: No target date or release window is stated; the Implementation Plan's five items are all unstarted and unscheduled (`brd/brd.md` Implementation Plan, Q15).

decisionsNeeded: Hosting surface: confirm website-customer-portal as the host for both pages, as the architect notes [A1] and the spike [R6] point to, against its known state (Angular 21 / Node 22, SSR disabled, 16 open Snyk criticals under CP-51568) [R23, R24].

Aggregate data source: direct retrieval (real-time, added PROD load the Data team wants to avoid) versus BI Platform (no PROD load, daily freshness, another team's resources) versus a materialized summary not proposed by any source [R6].

Owning service for the aggregate query: customer-service-v2, which owns the agreement domain SQL per the recorded convention [R8 Approach 4, R10], versus customer-service (the portal's current downstream, but the service being migrated away from [R29]) versus the BI Platform.

Transport path: whether customer-portal calls the aggregate endpoint through a new api-gateway route or reaches the service directly — the portal's recorded downstreams do not include api-gateway [R23].
Feature flag: reuse ambassador-upgrade-agreements-enabled [R2] or create a new flag for the reporting surface.
Scope of FR8 (record-level list) and, with it, the data classification, retention, and export controls of the feature.
How an ambassador who exercised the 30-day written opt-out is counted — not accepted, or a distinct state not modelled today [R32].
conflicts: Scope conflict: architect notes ask for the report to sit next to customer-specific agreements, implying the per-customer view is part of this work [A1]; the BRD excludes individual lookup as CP-50908's scope [B1 §Out of Scope, R4]. Drafted as in-scope-for-placement with the delivery question raised as Q1, not resolved.

Freshness versus load: BRD requirement 6 asks for data on an as-needed basis [B1 §Requirements 6]; the BI Platform option only refreshes once a day [R6 Business Intelligence Platform], while the direct-retrieval option meets it but adds PROD database load the Data team wants to avoid [R6 Direct Retrieval].

Platform direction versus host choice: the customer-portal host [A1, R6, R23] sits outside the reporting-service path that now serves all Virtual Office reports [R21, R28]; no decision record covers where a Legal-facing compliance report belongs. Recorded as a departure to confirm, not asserted as convention-compliant.

Service-ownership convention: adding reporting reads to customer-service (Node) would contradict the migration direction in the legacy-migration AAD [R29 §Service Selection]; the design therefore proposes customer-service-v2, following the domain-ownership rule in the decision record [R8 Approach 4]. Pending Q6.

Data-accuracy conflicts with counting: CP-51265 records duplicate CustomerAgreementTypeIDs for D2A enrollees [R33] and CP-51058 (Won't Do) records Arizona agreements applied to non-AZ customers [R34]; naive counts and state filters would be wrong. Raised as Q7 and as NFR 'Data accuracy caveats'.

changes: Created aad/aad.md as a first draft with all template sections in order, plus Open Questions and Sources appendices.

Overview and System Overview built from the delivered PLAN-818 architecture [R7, R10, R14, R16, R17] plus the architect's hosting direction [A1] and the spike's finding that aggregate progress has no reusable basis [R6].

Design presents the spike's two data-source options as an explicit tradeoff rather than choosing [R6], adds a third (materialized summary) clearly labelled as unsupported by any source, and a second tradeoff on which service owns the aggregate query [R8, R29].

High-Level Architecture Mermaid flowchart plus a change table covering every system in the System Overview; two Mermaid sequence diagrams (aggregate report and per-customer lookup), both with failure branches.
Functional requirements traced one-to-one to BRD requirements 1-7, with BRD requirement 8 carried as candidate FR8 and flagged undesigned.

Non-functional requirements drawn from the recorded conventions: PROD-load constraint [R6], no coupling to the login path [R7], Istio/Spring Boot/api-contracts conventions [R29], no new dependency on reports-service-v3 [R21].
Security threat model records seven risks with mitigations, including the customer-portal Snyk criticals [R23] and the risk of misleading figures relied on in litigation [R16].
Compliance section records the 30-day written opt-out as an unmodelled third state [R32] and the US-Ambassador population scope question [R32, B1 Q8].
Data Identification labels every proposed field and response shape as proposed; no schema change is claimed as required.
Eighteen open questions recorded, six marked blocking; all BRD open questions still relevant to the design were carried forward rather than answered.

memoryChanges: scope: New AAD accepted: Ambassador Agreement Acceptance Reporting (`aad/aad.md`) — adds an aggregate agreement-acceptance reporting surface for Legal/Compliance on top of the existing PLAN-818 acceptance record.
system: website-customer-portal named as the proposed host for the aggregate Agreement Progress page and the per-customer agreements section (`aad/aad.md` §System Overview, §Design).

system: Systems entering scope: customer-service-v2 (proposed owner of the aggregate query), customer-service (reused unchanged), api-gateway, ThatOtherGuy database, PlexusSync, Okta, LaunchDarkly, Contentful NextJS space; BI Platform conditional on the data-source option (`aad/aad.md` §System Overview, §High-Level Architecture).

interface: Proposed new read-only aggregate coverage endpoint on customer-service-v2, published in api-contracts, with a proposed response shape (agreementTypeId, version, requiredCount, acceptedCount, notAcceptedCount, coveragePercent, asOf) (`aad/aad.md` §Design, §Data models).
decision: Reporting will not use reports-service-v3, which is being decommissioned under CP-51485/CP-51441 (`aad/aad.md` §Problem statement, §Non-Functional Requirements).

decision: No schema change and no write path: the design reads the existing CustomerAgreement, CustomerAgreementType, and CustomerAgreementRequirement tables read-only (`aad/aad.md` §Data flow, §Data models).

convention: Conventions carried into this design: api-gateway authenticates and forwards while the domain service owns the SQL; new Java work follows the Spring Boot layered/api-contracts/Istio/Micrometer conventions of the legacy-migration AAD; LaunchDarkly gates new surfaces; Dynatrace is the monitoring standard (`aad/aad.md` §Non-Functional Requirements, §Design, §Monitoring and Observability).

data: Known data defects that distort acceptance counting are recorded as constraints: D2A duplicate agreement-type acceptance sets (CP-51265) and Arizona-scoped agreements applied to non-AZ customers (CP-51058) (`aad/aad.md` §Non-Functional Requirements, Q7).

dependency: Dependencies recorded: accepted BRD `brd/brd.md`; CP-51264 spike (page 5454659585); terms-gate AAD (page 5302779911) and its decision records; PLAN-818 release plan; customer-portal Alive plan (page 5490999297) and CP-51568 Snyk remediation; legacy Node→Java migration AAD (page 5193105409) (`aad/aad.md` §References).

decision: Two data-source options remain open and unchosen — direct retrieval from ThatOtherGuy/PlexusSync versus the BI Platform, with a third materialized-summary option recorded; the choice blocks the design (`aad/aad.md` Q2).
